cleanIntro: This book is shared by four different Sako rifles — the 90, the S20, the Quad and the Finnfire II — and it warns on its own opening page that not everything in it applies to yours. The steps below are the ones scoped to the Sako 90: it has a bolt shroud RELEASE that the S20 does not, its magazine loads from the top rather than under the lips, its magazine has to be tipped in before the release will open, and it is the only one of the four whose magazine teardown the manual documents. The field strip is magazine out, bolt out; the barrelled action comes out of the stock on two Torx T25 screws when you need to go further. Sako's own cleaning interval is aggressive — corrosion can start inside 24 hours, stainless and All-weather rifles included.

steps.title: This book covers four rifles — work the Sako 90 parts only
steps.action: Before you follow any procedure here, check it is scoped to the 90. The manual states plainly that it applies to the 90, the S20, the Quad and the Finnfire II together, and that you will meet material that does not apply to your rifle. Sections headed for the S20 or the Quad are not alternative ways to do the same job on a 90 — they describe different hardware.
steps.prose: This matters most at the bolt and the magazine, where the three actions genuinely differ.
steps.quote: This manual applies to all Sako 90, S20, Quad and Finnfire II models and includes explanations of standard as well as optional equipment. As a result, you may encounter material in this manual that is not applicable to your specific Sako model.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Introduction, p.10
steps.warn: This manual does not apply only to the Sako 90. Read the model name on each instruction before you follow it.

steps.title: Magazine out — on the Sako 90 you tip it in first
steps.action: Press the front of the magazine inward and, at the same time, push the release button backwards. That inward tip is the part people miss: on the 90 the magazine has to be pressed in before the catch will let go, and pulling straight down on a magazine that has not been tipped just feels jammed. Sako rimfires and the S20 do not need the lift, which is exactly why the instruction is written with that exception attached.
steps.prose: Do the magazine before the chamber. A chamber cleared with a loaded magazine still in place re-feeds itself the moment the bolt closes.
steps.caution: The no-lift shortcut belongs to Sako rimfires and the Sako S20, NOT to the Sako 90.
steps.quote: • Remove the magazine by depressing the front part of the magazine inward and simultaneously pushing the release button backwards (fig. 7). On Sako rimfires and Sako S20 the magazine does not have to be lifted before opening the magazine release.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Load Check, p.12

steps.title: Bolt back, chamber checked, then decock
steps.action: With the safety forward, lift the bolt handle and draw it back to pull any chambered round out, then look into the chamber. When the rifle is genuinely empty, close the bolt, point it somewhere safe and pull the trigger to let the firing pin down — Sako wants the 90 stored and handled decocked, and the pin will only come down with the bolt closed. Trying to decock with the bolt open achieves nothing.
steps.prose: The full unload also empties the magazine itself: thumb each cartridge rim forward and tip it up with the index finger, one at a time.
steps.quote: • Keeping the firearm pointed in a safe direction, disengage the safety by pushing it forward (red dot not visible). • Lift and pull back the bolt to extract the live cartridge from the chamber. • Remove the magazine by pushing the magazine release button (fig. 7).
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Unloading the Rifle, p.14
steps.warn: The firing pin can be decocked only when the bolt is in the closed position.

steps.title: Everything below happens on an empty rifle
steps.action: Sako states the precondition once and applies it to every strip and service procedure in the book: chamber empty, receiver empty, magazine empty, and you prove it by sighting down the barrel from the rear of the receiver with the bolt out. That last part is the useful bit — with the bolt gone you get a clean line through the bore and can settle the obstruction question at the same time.
steps.prose: Do it over a table. Small parts that get away from you on a bolt-action rifle are usually the bolt stop pin.
steps.quote: All assembly, disassembly and maintenance procedures should be carried out with the firearm unloaded (cartridge chamber, receiver and magazine empty). Inspect the firearm by looking through barrel from the rear end of the receiver.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Assembly, Disassembly and Maintenance, Warning, p.10

steps.title: Bolt out of the receiver
steps.action: Lift the bolt handle, press the bolt stop button on the left of the receiver and draw the bolt fully out to the rear. Keep the button pressed for the whole travel; release it early and the bolt stops dead against it partway out. The bolt comes out cocked, so put it down somewhere it will not roll onto its lugs.
steps.prose: This is the whole of the Sako 90 field strip — a bolt gun with a detachable magazine has nothing else that comes off without tools.
steps.quote: • Remove the bolt by lifting the bolt handle, pressing the bolt stop button and completely pulling the bolt out of the receiver.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Load Check, p.12

steps.title: Look through the bore while the bolt is out
steps.action: With the bolt gone, hold the receiver up to the light and look straight through from the breech. You are looking for anything at all — Sako's wording is 'even minor ones', because a partial obstruction is the dangerous kind. If you find something, it does not get poked out or shot out: a gunsmith removes it and the rifle is inspected again before it is fired.
steps.prose: This is the one inspection that is easiest at exactly this point in the strip, which is why the manual attaches it to bolt removal.
steps.quote: • Look through the barrel from the rear and make sure there are no obstructions, even minor ones. • If an obstruction in the barrel is detected, a competent gunsmith must remove the obstruction.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Obstruction Check, p.12

steps.title: Barrelled action out of the stock — Torx T25, two screws
steps.action: If you need the action out, bolt and magazine come first, then both receiver fastening screws with a Torx T25 driver. The trigger guard pulls downwards once the screws are clear, and then the barrelled action lifts upwards out of the stock. Take the screws out fully rather than backing them off — a half-out screw is what marks the stock inletting when the action lifts.
steps.prose: This is the Sako 90 and Quad route. The S20 is a different animal here: its buttstock and fore-end come off the stock base on their own fastening screws, and that procedure does not belong to your rifle.
steps.caution: The pin in the bolt stop is preloaded by the spring. However, it may come out of the receiver, if the components are handled carelessly.
steps.quote: Remove the barreled receiver from the stock as follows (fig. 13): 1. Make sure that the rifle is not loaded with ammunition. 2. Remove the bolt and the magazine. 3. Remove the two receiver fastening screws (A) using a Torx T25 driver. 4. Remove the trigger guard by pulling it downwards. 5. Carefully pull the barreled receiver upwards out of the rifle.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Disassembly and Assembly of the Rifle Components — Barreled Receiver, p.16

steps.title: Rail and mount are model-scoped on the Sako 90
steps.action: If your strip is happening because you are changing optics, note what the 90 actually carries. Sako lists three rail standards across the four rifles in this book and the 90 is the only one offered with a 17mm dovetail, with a solid Picatinny rail as its other option. The 11mm dovetail belongs to the Quad and the Finnfire II — rings for those will not go on your receiver.
steps.prose: Optilock mounts are Sako's own; S20 mounts are a separate range and are not interchangeable with 90 mounts.
steps.quote: Sako rifles feature three different mounting rail options: • 17mm dovetail (Sako 90) • Solid Picatinny rail (Sako S20, Sako 90) • 11mm dovetail (Sako Quad and Finnfire II)
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Rifle Scope Assembly, p.14

steps.title: Clean it the day you shoot it — 24 hours is the window
steps.action: Sako's interval is right after use, and it applies even if you did not fire: handling alone is enough. Corrosion can begin within 24 hours on an uncleaned rifle, and the manual makes the point that a stainless or All-weather Sako 90 is not exempt from that. Use a CLP-type oil that cleans, lubricates and preserves, and support the rifle on its bipod while you work.
steps.prose: That 24-hour figure is the reason a rifle put away wet after a wet day is the commonest way a good barrel is spoiled.
steps.quote: Routine cleaning should always take place right after use of the rifle (even without shooting). Maintenance should not be neglected even in case of the "All-weather" or "Stainless" models. Corrosion can begin within 24 hours if the rifle is not cleaned after use.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Routine Cleaning and Maintenance, p.22

steps.title: Bore from the breech, one direction only
steps.action: Push-pull a bronze brush soaked in solvent through the bore ten to fifteen times to shift the bulk of the residue, using a rod guide so the rod does not drag on the bore or the receiver walls. Then run solvent-moistened felt pellets through, five to ten of them, replacing the pellet every pass and always working in the direction the bullet travels. A pellet that comes out clean is your finish line.
steps.prose: Finish with a pellet carrying rust-preventive oil and leave a thin film on the chamber — then remember to wipe that chamber dry before you shoot.
steps.caution: Lead bullets leave bore leading which raises pressure. Make sure to remove all chamber and bore lead accumulation after each use. DO NOT ever shoot with steel jacketed bullets!
steps.quote: 3. Use an absolutely straight, sturdy and smooth cleaning rod fitted with bronze bore brush soaked in bore solvent and push-pull it through the bore until major residue is removed (approx. 10-15 times).
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Routine Cleaning and Maintenance, step 3, p.23

steps.title: Bolt exterior, receiver interior, then a light oil film
steps.action: With the bolt still out, brush the firing residue off it with a small solvent-wetted brush and clean the inner surfaces of the receiver the same way. Wipe every surface where bolt and receiver touch with a very light coat of rust-preventive oil — light, because a heavy film here is what creeps into the bolt and dulls the firing pin. Wipe the stock dry, and check the receiver screws are still tight before you call it done.
steps.prose: Oil migrating into the bolt is the specific fault Sako gives as the reason to strip the bolt at all, so keeping it out is cheaper than dealing with it.
steps.quote: 6. Use a small solvent-wetted brush to clean the bolt from firing residue.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Routine Cleaning and Maintenance, step 6, p.23

steps.title: Sako 90 bolt: it has a shroud release the S20 does not
steps.action: If you go past bolt removal, the 90's teardown is its own. Press the bolt shroud release, then turn the shroud clockwise — counter-clockwise on left-hand rifles — until its notches clear the bolt body, holding it firmly the whole time because the firing pin spring is compressed behind it. The S20 has no release button and is simply turned, and the Quad uses a side pin instead; neither procedure works on your rifle.
steps.prose: And that is as far as it goes. Sako states the 90's bolt needs no further disassembly to be cleaned, so the shroud and firing pin assembly come off as a unit and stay a unit.
steps.quote: 2. SAKO 90: Push the bolt shroud release (A) and turn the bolt shroud (B) clockwise (LH models: counter-clockwise) until its locking notches are disengaged from the bolt body. Caution! Hold the bolt shroud tightly and watch out for flying parts as the firing pin spring has tension.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Bolt — SAKO 90/S20, step 2, p.17
steps.warn: The bolt should not require any further disassembly for cleaning purposes.

steps.title: Magazine service is a Sako 90 section — and so is magazine loading
steps.action: The magazine strip in this book is headed for the Sako 90 alone; no equivalent is published for the S20, the Quad or the Finnfire II. Loading is scoped the same way: on the 90 a cartridge goes onto the follower from the top of the magazine, while the S20, Quad and Finnfire II take it in front of the lips and slide it under them. If you have been shown the under-the-lips method on another Sako, it is not how yours loads.
steps.prose: That difference is why the 90's magazine also has to be tipped inward before the release will let it out.
steps.caution: • Sako 90: Place a cartridge on the magazine follower from the top of the magazine (fig. 8).
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Disassembly and Assembly of the Rifle Components — Magazine, p.17

steps.title: Trigger adjustment is model-scoped too — do not borrow the Quad's route
steps.action: Two things here belong to the 90 and two do not. Trigger blade horizontal position is adjustable on the Sako 90 and the S20 assemblies, so you can shift the blade a few millimetres either way on its fastening screw. Trigger pull weight on the 90 is reached with a Torx T25 through the trigger guard — you do not need the action out of the stock, and if a procedure tells you to pull the barrelled action to reach the screw, that instruction is written for a Quad or a Finnfire II.
steps.prose: Sear engagement and the safety are factory-set precision adjustments and are not yours at all; a replaced trigger, sear or safety catch means the safety must be readjusted by the manufacturer.
steps.caution: On some Sako models (Sako Quad, Finnfire II) access to the adjustment screw requires removal of the barreled action from the stock.
steps.quote: On some trigger assemblies (Sako 90, S20) you can adjust the horizontal position of the trigger blade.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Trigger Blade Position, p.16

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Magazine out, bolt out, bore looked through, and the barrelled action off the stock if you went that far. That is the Sako 90's published strip — there is nothing else on this rifle that comes apart without going into Deep Clean. Deep Clean covers the bolt shroud teardown, which on the 90 uses a shroud release the S20 does not have, and the magazine strip, which the manual scopes to the 90 alone.
steps.prose: Before it goes back together, remember the trigger is a factory-set precision mechanism: pull weight is adjustable through the trigger guard, but sear engagement and the safety are not yours to alter.
steps.quote: It is advisable to carry out the disassembly operations over a table to catch components should they drop.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Disassembly and Assembly of the Rifle Components, p.16

deepSteps.title: Strip the bolt only when oil has got into it
deepSteps.action: Sako's own position is that the 90's bolt does not normally need taking apart. The trigger for doing it is a bolt that has taken on too much oil and lost its snap, and that matters most in cold weather where surplus oil thickens and slows the firing pin. Do not make it routine — the reassembly has a cocking step that has to be got right every time.
deepSteps.prose: If you have been generous with rust-preventive oil on the bolt exterior, this is the bill for it.
deepSteps.quote: Generally, disassembling the bolt is not necessary. If you have reason to believe that too much oil may have penetrated the bolt, you should clean it in order to retain its smooth operation. This is particularly important if you use the rifle in cold or harsh weather.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Disassembly and Assembly of the Rifle Components — Bolt, p.17

deepSteps.title: SAKO 90 bolt shroud — press the release, then turn clockwise
deepSteps.action: The 90 has a bolt shroud release the S20 does not: press it, then turn the shroud clockwise (counter-clockwise on left-hand rifles) until its locking notches come clear of the bolt body. Hold the shroud firmly the whole time. The firing pin spring is compressed behind it and the moment the notches disengage, that spring is trying to launch the shroud out of your hand.
deepSteps.prose: The S20 has no release button and is simply turned — do not go looking for a button on an S20 or expect an S20's procedure to work on your 90.
deepSteps.quote: 2. SAKO 90: Push the bolt shroud release (A) and turn the bolt shroud (B) clockwise (LH models: counter-clockwise) until its locking notches are disengaged from the bolt body. Caution! Hold the bolt shroud tightly and watch out for flying parts as the firing pin spring has tension.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Bolt — SAKO 90/S20, step 2, p.17
deepSteps.warn: Firing pin spring under tension. Eye protection, and control the shroud with both hands.

deepSteps.title: That is as far as the bolt comes apart
deepSteps.action: Once the shroud and firing pin assembly are off the bolt body, stop. Sako states that nothing further needs to come apart for cleaning, and going deeper on a 90 bolt means dismantling the firing pin assembly itself, which is spring-loaded and has no user-serviceable parts inside. Clean the bolt body, the locking lugs and the bolt face as they are.
deepSteps.prose: The Quad is stripped differently again — a side pin is pushed out of its shroud — which is another reason not to borrow a procedure across models in this book.
deepSteps.quote: The bolt should not require any further disassembly for cleaning purposes.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Bolt — SAKO 90/S20, p.17

deepSteps.title: Rebuild the bolt cocking-piece first
deepSteps.action: Put the firing pin assembly, spring and spring guide back with the shroud so the cocking piece sits opposite the bolt handle and the shroud's locking notches line up with the rear of the bolt body. Push the shroud against the bolt and turn it counter-clockwise until the cocking piece cam stops in the cocking notch — on the Sako 90 the shroud release snaps into its own notch at the same moment, and that click is your confirmation the two locked together.
deepSteps.prose: If the release does not drop in, the shroud is not fully seated; press harder before turning further.
deepSteps.aside: Left-hand rifles reverse the direction: clockwise to reassemble.
deepSteps.quote: 1. Put the firing pin assembly with the spring and
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Bolt — SAKO 90/S20, reassembly step 1, p.17

deepSteps.title: Magazine teardown — this section is the Sako 90's alone
deepSteps.action: The manual documents a magazine strip for the 90 and for no other rifle in the book. Depress the rear of the follower with a soft-pointed tool so the follower and spring can come out of the box. Wash the box, spring and follower in warm soapy water or solvent, oil all three lightly, then reverse the steps and check the spring is sitting the way the figure shows before you trust it.
deepSteps.prose: A spring reinstalled a quarter-turn out feeds fine on the bench and fails on the last round.
deepSteps.caution: Loading is also 90-specific: "• Sako 90: Place a cartridge on the magazine follower from the top of the magazine (fig. 8)." The S20, Quad and Finnfire II slide the cartridge under the lips instead.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Disassembly and Assembly of the Rifle Components — Magazine, p.17

deepSteps.title: Periodic service — once a year, and grease three surfaces
deepSteps.action: At least annually, or sooner under heavy use, do the routine clean and then go further: pull copper fouling from the bore, strip the bolt, brush it with solvent and lubricate it lightly, and put grease specifically on the locking lug surfaces, the camming slope and the head of the cocking piece. Those three are the loaded sliding contacts in a Sako 90 bolt and they are the ones that gall if they run dry.
deepSteps.prose: Reassemble and then actually test the extractor and ejector by hand rather than assuming they survived the wash.
deepSteps.quote: 5. Disassemble the bolt as instructed in the manual, clean the dirt with solvent-wetted brush and lightly lubricate surfaces with protective oil. Lightly grease the locking lug surfaces (A, fig. 5), camming slope (B) and head of the cocking piece (C).
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Periodic Maintenance, step 5, p.23

deepSteps.title: Put it away dry, and not in a soft case
deepSteps.action: Before the rifle goes into storage, check it over and make sure it is perfectly dry, and take the suppressor off the muzzle if one is fitted — a can left on traps moisture against the threads. Do not store a Sako 90 in a leather or fabric case; those materials hold water even when they feel bone dry, and they hold it against the metal.
deepSteps.prose: Ammunition goes in a separate secure place, and local law on firearm storage takes precedence over anything the manual says.
deepSteps.quote: Before storage, always check the condition of the rifle and ensure that it is perfectly dry. Moreover, remember to remove the suppressor from the barrel (if fitted) before storage.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL / KÄYTTÖOHJEKIRJA / BRUKSANVISNING / MANUALE DI ISTRUZIONE / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUEL DE L'UTILISATEUR / MANUAL DE UTILIZACIÓN — 90  S20  QUAD  FINNFIRE II — S3A11011/ 3.5 — Storage, p.23
deepSteps.warn: Do not store the rifle in a leather or fabric case. These materials attract moisture, even though they may appear to be perfectly dry.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Bronze brush with solvent, push-pull 10-15 times, using a rod guide
Felt pellets with solvent, 5-10 passes, fresh pellet each time, in the direction of bullet travel only
Nylon brush or chamber pellet for the chamber
Finish with a rust-preventive pellet; leave a thin oil film on the chamber and WIPE IT DRY before shooting
Remove all lead accumulation after each use if shooting lead bullets

cleaning.name: BOLT & RECEIVER
tasks: Small solvent-wetted brush over the bolt to lift firing residue
Clean the inner receiver surfaces with pellet and/or brush
Very light rust-preventive oil on every bolt/receiver contact surface
Annually: grease the locking lug surfaces, camming slope and cocking piece head

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE — SAKO 90 ONLY
tasks: Depress the rear of the follower with a soft-pointed tool to release follower and spring
Wash box, spring and follower in warm soapy water or solvent
Light oil on all parts before reassembly
Check the spring sits as figure 16 shows before refitting

cleaning.name: STOCK & SCREWS
tasks: Wipe the stock dry; oil-finished wooden stocks get a good stock oil
Check receiver screw tightness every clean
Store dry, suppressor removed, never in a leather or fabric case

reassembly: Rebuild the bolt: firing pin assembly, spring and guide into the shroud with the cocking piece opposite the bolt handle, shroud notches aligned to the rear of the bolt body.
Push the shroud home and turn it counter-clockwise (clockwise on left-hand rifles) until the cocking piece cam stops in the cocking notch and the Sako 90's shroud release clicks into its notch.
If the action came out of the stock: seat the barrelled receiver, refit the trigger guard, and run both receiver fastening screws in with the Torx T25 driver.
Insert the bolt into the receiver and close it.
Refit the magazine — on the Sako 90 it tips in at the front before the catch takes it.
Wipe the oil film out of the chamber before any cartridge goes near it.
fncheck: Sako's own post-service check is "6. Assemble the bolt and check the function of different parts (incl. extractors and ejectors)." (Periodic Maintenance, p.23). On an empty Sako 90 that means: bolt cycles and locks down without drag; the extractor claw springs back when pushed; the ejector moves freely; the safety engages with the red dot hidden and locks both the trigger and the closed bolt; and the firing pin decocks with the bolt closed. Note that "Long term dry firing may damage the bolt." (p.13) — use a snap cap if you want to test the trigger repeatedly. Also confirm the receiver screws are tight and the magazine seats and releases cleanly with the front-tip-in motion the 90 requires.
